title: Best Tablet Under ₹10,000 in India (2026): 5 Picks For Reading, Study & Streaming
description: Compare the best tablets under Rs 10,000 in India by screen, battery, RAM, and use case — pick the right budget tablet for reading, study, or streaming.
short_desc: Five budget tablets under ₹10,000 for Indian buyers, ranked by screen quality, battery, and use case.
keywords: tablet for reading and study India
Lenovo vs Samsung vs Redmi tablet

headings.text: What actually matters in a tablet under ₹10,000

cta.headline: Need a larger tablet for note-taking or sketching?
cta.sub: Our tablet guide for note-taking covers 10-13 inch tablets with stylus support, including the Samsung Galaxy Tab S FE and Lenovo Tab P series.

tldr_pick: The Redmi Pad SE 8.7" (Helio G85, 4GB/64GB) is the best tablet under ₹10,000 in India for most buyers in 2026: an 8.7-inch HD+ screen with 90Hz refresh, MediaTek Helio G85 chip, 4GB RAM, 64GB storage, a 6650 mAh battery, and Xiaomi's widest service network.
key_takeaways: 8-inch is the sweet spot for portability; 10-inch for media — sub-8-inch tablets feel cramped; above 10-inch they are bulky for one-hand reading.
4GB RAM is the floor; 3GB stutters on Android 14+ — sub-₹10,000 tablets now ship with 4GB as standard; avoid 3GB models.
Wi-Fi only is fine for home use; 4G SIM adds ₹1,500-₹2,500 for on-the-go connectivity — buy 4G only if you'll use the tablet outside Wi-Fi often.
Android 14+ with 2 years of updates is the right benchmark — Android 12 tablets are already one update behind.
who_for: Indian buyers looking for a budget tablet for reading, online classes, streaming, or light gaming under ₹10,000. Not aimed at professional drawing or productivity work — those need 10-inch+ tablets with stylus support above ₹15,000.
methodology: We compared 7 popular budget tablets sold in India in 2026 in the ₹7,000-₹10,000 band against three use cases: reading (screen quality, weight, battery), online classes (camera, mic, speaker), and streaming (screen resolution, Wi-Fi stability). Pricing is the current normal sale price on Amazon India and Flipkart; verify the exact model code on the listing before purchase.

faq.q: Is 4GB RAM enough on a budget tablet?
faq.a: Yes for reading, streaming, and online classes — the daily-use apps that most budget tablet buyers use. 3GB RAM stutters on Android 14+ when you switch between 3-4 apps; 4GB is comfortable. Above 4GB only matters for gaming or split-screen multitasking, which budget tablets don't handle well anyway.

faq.q: Do I need 4G SIM on a budget tablet?
faq.a: Only if you'll use the tablet outside Wi-Fi regularly — commuting, travel, or outdoor study. For home use, Wi-Fi only is fine and saves ₹1,500-₹2,500. Most budget tablets have a Wi-Fi-only variant and a 4G variant at the same screen size; check the listing carefully.

8-inch is the sweet spot for one-hand reading, online classes, and commuting. 10-inch is better for split-screen multitasking, sketching, and watching video with two people. Below 8-inch, the screen feels cramped for reading. Above 10-inch, the tablet is bulky for one-hand use.

faq.q: How long does a budget tablet's battery last?
faq.a: Most budget tablets in this price band have a 5,000-6,650 mAh battery, which translates to 7-10 hours of mixed use (reading + streaming + light apps). The Redmi Pad SE leads with 6,650 mAh; the Lenovo Tab M9 trails at 5,100 mAh. For comparison, an iPad Mini lasts about 10 hours, but costs 4-5x as much.

faq.q: Can I use a budget tablet for online classes?
faq.a: Yes — 8-inch budget tablets handle Zoom / Google Meet / Teams classes fine. Look for a front camera of 5MP or higher (most have 5MP or 8MP), a microphone array that cancels background noise, and Wi-Fi 5 (ac) or later for stable video. The Samsung Galaxy Tab A9 has the best front camera in this list; the Redmi Pad SE has the best battery for long class sessions.
